summary: A 60-foot Civilian Conservation Corps timber tower built in 1938 on the Unity Ranger Station compound in Oregon, kept for emergency use.

facts.design: 60-foot treated timber tower with a 6x6 observation cab and a wooden water tank just below the cab
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Wallowa-Whitman National Forest

access.note: On a working Forest Service compound that is open only in summer. Sources describe the tower as available for emergencies. No source says the public may climb it.

visit.trail_note: On the south side of Main Street (U.S. 26) in Unity. Trees make it hard to see from the road.

events.note: 60-foot timber tower with 6x6 cab and water tank, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps
Newspaper notice says the new Unity tower was completed in August 1939, 63 ft to the floor; conflicts with the 1938 date
Emergency fire lookout manned during high-hazard days (Record-Courier, July 1962)
Unity Ranger Station compound, including the lookout, added to the National Register
District headquarters moved to Baker City after the district merged with two others
Full-time visitor center at the station ended
Registered July 6, 2022 as US 1645, OR 163; nominated by Brad Eells

corrections.why: Every source gives the tower as 60 feet (18 m). The current 1.8 is not supported.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia gives a 7-by-7-foot cab. The NHLR entry, the Oregon lookouts site and firelookout.com give 6 by 6. The story reports the 6x6 figure and notes the Wikipedia figure.

Four sources date the tower to 1938. An August 1939 newspaper notice reports a new Unity tower completed at 63 feet to the floor. The record keeps 1938 as the construction year and treats the 1939 item as a conflicting completion report.

sources.title: Unity Ranger Station Fire Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 1.8 corrected to 18 m. NHLR, Wikipedia and the Oregon site agree on a 1938 CCC build; a 1939 newspaper notice reports completion at 63 ft. Cab size conflicts (6x6 vs 7x7). Wikipedia cites the 1986 NRHP nomination, which was not read. Living New Deal returned HTTP 403 and was not used. No notable fire found. Current status rests on 2018 and 2022 sources; no later check.
